before:
Cliff Path Trust - Autumn Maintenance Report

Work parties met on six Saturdays between September and November, with an average turnout of nine volunteers. The season's schedule followed the ordering agreed at the spring meeting: boardwalk repairs are attended to before stile replacement, and stile replacement before waymarker repainting, with any remaining hours given to drainage clearance. All four kinds of work remain open to volunteers at every session, and nothing has been withdrawn from the list. Materials were drawn from the Ferry Lane store as usual. The warden notes that a wet October reduced the days available, and that the drainage backlog therefore carried over into the winter book. Tools were returned complete on each occasion.

before:
Pottery Shed - Kiln Room Controller Settings

This sheet lists the values entered on the controller after the January service, and supersedes the sheet taped inside the door. The upper firing limit is set at 1,180 degrees, the ramp is set at 90 degrees an hour to 600, and the holding period is forty minutes. The room sensor is polled every thirty seconds. Night-time ventilation may be run at the low setting whenever a firing has finished after eight in the evening, and the extract interlock stays armed until the room falls below 40 degrees. Keys to the panel are kept in the office tin. Values are altered by the shed steward only.

before:
Village Pump Trust - Committee Minutes, Item 4

Item 4: failure of the borehole pump on 3 February. The engineer's visit note was read to the meeting. The failure was caused by a seized bearing on the drive shaft, following ingress of grit through the worn upper seal. Repair took two days and the standpipe was closed for that period. Costs of four hundred and twelve pounds were met from the maintenance fund, leaving eleven hundred and eighty. The committee asked that the seal be inspected at each quarterly visit and that a spare be held in the shed. Item 4 was closed with thanks to the two members who carried water to the top cottages.

before:
Sluice House Operating Manual - Section 2, Header Tank

Section 2 covers the header tank on the roof of the sluice house and the gravity feed to the wash-down hoses. The header tank holds 1,200 litres when filled to the overflow lip, and refills from the mains through a float valve on the north side. A full tank runs both hoses for roughly forty minutes at normal pressure. The sight glass is read from the walkway, where the painted marks stand at quarter intervals. In frost the feed line is drained at the low-point cock beside the ladder. Inspection of the lid seal falls due each March, and the ladder anchors are checked at the same visit.

before:
Lending Library - Accession Catalogue Working Notes

These notes describe how donated books reach the shelves, and are kept at the counter for the use of relief volunteers. Each new book is stamped on the title page, then entered with its accession number in the ledger, then jacketed, and then shelved. Books judged unsuitable for lending are set aside for the summer sale table rather than entered at all. The ledger is a bound book, not a card tray, and no entry is ever erased; corrections are made with a struck line and initials. Donations arrive in the porch box and are cleared each Tuesday. The stamp and the jacketing film live in the second drawer.

before:
Boatyard Notice - Winter Storage Charges

Notice to owners: the hard-standing opens on 1 October and the last lift is on 20 December. Charges for winter storage are worked out from the yard's length-based tariff, at the posted figure for each foot over all, with cradle hire added separately. Invoices are issued monthly in arrears and are payable within twenty-eight days. Owners doing their own work on the hard must sign the yard book each morning. Pressure washing is included with the lift if taken on the same day, otherwise it is charged at the standing hourly figure. Masts are stored in the rack at the owner's risk, and the yard's cover does not extend to them.

before:
Field Study Centre Handbook - Specimen Labels

Every specimen leaving the centre carries a label written in pencil on card, since ink fails in spirit. The label gives the collector, the collection number, the site code and the date, in that order, with the fields separated by commas and a single space. The date is always written with the month in Roman numerals so that day and month cannot be confused. Labels are cut from the card stock kept in the flat drawer, and the pencil is an F grade. A label that becomes illegible is copied out and both are kept together in the tube. Loans out of the centre are noted in the day book.

before:
Ferry Slipway - Dogs at the Waiting Pontoon

This note sets out the position on dogs at the slipway and the waiting pontoon, following complaints received over the summer season. Dogs may be brought onto the waiting pontoon provided they are held on a short lead and are not left tied to the rail. Assistance dogs are unaffected by anything written here. Fouling is to be cleared by the handler and the bagged waste placed in the bin at the head of the slip, never in the water. The crew may decline carriage on any sailing where the deck is crowded. Notices to this effect are posted at the ticket hut and at the top of the ramp.
